cases.title: The star that glowed before it dimmed
cases.hook: In 2018 this Sun-like star started glowing in the infrared. Three years later it began to fade. Something hot came first.

cases.title: The most mysterious star in the galaxy (allegedly)
cases.hook: Boyajian's Star: irregular dips of up to 22% that no planet could make. Aliens were proposed. Dust was found.

cases.title: The eclipse that comes back every 5.6 years
cases.hook: Every 2,050 days something dark and enormous passes in front of this star. In November 2025 it blocked 73% of the light. In 2014 it blocked 48%.

cases.title: The star that smokes
cases.hook: For months it shines steadily; then it vanishes by eight magnitudes, as if someone blew out a candle. It makes its own soot.

cases.title: Breathing in, breathing out
cases.hook: A giant star swelling and shrinking every 14 months, brightening a thousandfold. Strange to the eye, ordinary to astrophysics.

cases.title: The star that won't stay quiet
cases.hook: Every few weeks, for a century of amateur records, it leaps fiftyfold in brightness in a day. Something is feeding on its neighbour.

cases.title: The young star that went dark in 2011
cases.hook: A famous, well-behaved young star that suddenly dimmed by two magnitudes and stayed dim for a decade.

cases.title: Control A
cases.hook: A quiet G star in TESS's continuous viewing zone. Used in trials as a canvas for planted artifacts.

cases.title: Control B
cases.hook: A quiet G star in TESS's continuous viewing zone. Nothing to see here, and that is the test.

cases.title: The young star nobody classified
cases.hook: Listed as a 'suspected variable' for decades. Gaia, ZTF and NEOWISE agree: a young star in Perseus whose own disk keeps blotting it out.

cases.title: A binary hiding behind the wrong period
cases.hook: Gaia's catalogue gave it a 53-minute period. The real one is 2.53 days, and nobody had written it down.

cases.title: The invisible companion that wasn't
cases.hook: We thought something the size of the Sun was blocking this star every 2.38 days without giving off any light. Our own referee agent found the mistake in 30 minutes.

cases.title: An infrared excess that appeared in 2018
cases.hook: A K dwarf 250 parsecs away was a bare photosphere for four years. Then, between two NEOWISE visits in 2018, 1000 K dust appeared around it, and it is still there.

cases.title: The star that vanished for three months
cases.hook: In spring 2017 a G dwarf 420 parsecs away disappeared, more than 99% of its light gone for nearly two months and dimmed for about 95 days. Afterwards it began to glow in the infrared. Nobody noticed.

cases.title: A dust-shrouded star in a star-forming region goes dark for two to three weeks every 385.7 days
cases.hook: Found in Oddsky hunt H-0004 while looking for R CrB declines. Tisserand+2020 WISE candidate 2682 (2MASS J18205507-1340452), 4 arcsec from IRAS 18180-1342: steady to 0.1-0.2 mag, then four sharp 1.5-2.2 mag eclipses in four consecutive years, deeper in blue, on a strict 385.7-day period. Listed as a 'dubious' ATLAS variable and a Gaia DR2 long-period-variable candidate; the eclipses themselves were never reported.

cases.title: A red giant toward the Galactic anticentre brightened sevenfold for a few weeks in 2017: a microlensing event
cases.hook: Found in Oddsky hunt H-0007 as a one-visit, colour-neutral 2.7x brightening in NEOWISE (2017 Aug 27-28); ATLAS shows a single smooth event peaking near 2017 Sep 16. Not in VSX, TNS, the Gaia alerts or Gaia DR3.

cases.title: A halo giant brightened at least 2.4 times in March 2020 and faded over six months: a microlensing event
cases.hook: Found in Oddsky hunt H-0007 among faint stars: a one-visit, colour-neutral 2x brightening in NEOWISE (2020 Apr 9-10). ATLAS shows one smooth event, x2.4 on Mar 11 and within 2% of normal by October; ZTF catches the tail. The peak fell in a gap. Not in VSX, TNS, SIMBAD or the Gaia alerts.

cases.title: A star in Serpens brightened fivefold over four months in 2022: an apparently unreported microlensing event
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 as a colour-neutral 3.5x brightening in NEOWISE (2022 Aug 31). ATLAS shows one smooth, symmetric event peaking near 2022 Sep 19 at about 5x, lasting months. Not in TNS, the Gaia alerts, the KMTNet or OGLE lists, the ZTF microlensing catalogues, SIMBAD, VSX or ADS full text.

cases.title: A bulge giant in Sagittarius brightened by half for four months in 2022: a blended microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 as a colour-neutral 1.5x brightening in NEOWISE (2022 Sep 8). ATLAS and ZTF show one smooth event peaking in late August 2022, equal from g to 4.6 microns. ALeRCE classifies the ZTF object as LPV/YSO.

cases.title: A star in Scorpius brightened ninefold in August 2017 and Gaia never alerted: a microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 (NEOWISE x8 in W1 and W2 on 2017 Aug 17). ATLAS shows one smooth, achromatic event peaking in mid-August 2017; a point lens with annual parallax fits. Gaia scanned it during the event without an alert; DR4 will show what it saw.

cases.title: A G = 15 star in Scorpius brightened nearly eightfold for months in 2018: a long microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 (NEOWISE: x1.4 on 2018 Mar 16 and x3.0 on 2018 Aug 27, equal in W1 and W2). ATLAS shows a smooth x7.7 event peaking 2018 Jul 11-14; a lens fits only with annual parallax, and the timescale is poorly constrained.

cases.title: A star in Crux was seven times brighter on one NEOWISE visit in 2018: a test for Gaia DR4
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunts H-0008/H-0009: x6.9 in both W1 and W2 on 2018 Jul 14, every other visit quiet. No optical survey covered it; Gaia DR4 is the second instrument.

cases.title: A star in Norma brightened eightfold over two NEOWISE visits in 2017: a test for Gaia DR4
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0009: x1.8 on 2017 Mar 1, x8.3 on 2017 Aug 15, in both W1 and W2, quiet before and after. No optical survey covered it; Gaia DR4 is the second instrument.

cases.title: A star in Centaurus was 2.5 times brighter on one NEOWISE visit in 2015: a test for Gaia DR4
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunts H-0008/H-0009: x2.5 in both W1 and W2 on 2015 Aug 1, every other visit quiet. No optical survey covered it; Gaia DR4 is the second instrument.

cases.title: A star in Norma was 2.3 times brighter on one NEOWISE visit in 2017: a test for Gaia DR4
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunts H-0008/H-0009: x2.3 in both W1 and W2 on 2017 Aug 12, every other visit quiet. No optical survey covered it; Gaia DR4 is the second instrument.

cases.title: A star in Scorpius brightened sixfold in 2015, seen by NEOWISE and Gaia: an apparently unreported microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunts H-0008/H-0009 (NEOWISE x4.5 on 2015 Sep 7). Gaia DR3 epoch photometry shows the same event, x5.9 seven days earlier and fading over six weeks, equal in BP and RP. Gaia's own classifier labels the star MICROLENSING.

cases.title: A star in Sagittarius brightened 2.6 times in September 2015, equally in Gaia and NEOWISE: a microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunts H-0008/H-0009 (NEOWISE x2.7 on 2015 Sep 15). Gaia DR3 epoch photometry shows x2.6 nine days earlier and twenty days later, equal in G and RP. Gaia's own classifier labels the star MICROLENSING.

cases.title: A star in Sagittarius brightened briefly in March 2022 while OGLE was paused: a short microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 (NEOWISE x2.2 on 2022 Mar 19). ATLAS shows a sharp, symmetric event peaking on 2022 Mar 25 and lasting about two weeks, the same in optical and infrared. OGLE was paused and the star is outside KMTNet's fields.

cases.title: A star in Serpens brightened by half in March 2016, equally in Gaia's three bands: a microlensing candidate
cases.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0009 (NEOWISE x1.6 on 2016 Mar 21). Gaia DR3 epoch photometry shows x1.5 sixteen days earlier and x1.4 fifteen days later, equal in G, BP and RP, fading by late April. Gaia's classifier labels the star MICROLENSING.

cases.title: An infrared flare in the galaxy NGC 3239 in 2020 that no optical survey saw: probably a very dusty nova
cases.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's mid-infrared difference imaging of 318 nearby galaxies (hunt H-0012) and reported as AT 2020afkm: a flare peaking in 2020 November with no optical alert. Hubble caught a faint point source 85 days later that has since vanished, and JWST found warm dust at the same spot in 2024. K. De's group, who flagged it independently in 2022, favour a very dusty nova from a near-infrared spectrum taken during the outburst.

cases.title: A hidden infrared source in NGC 2403 that has flared every 5.3 years since 2007: a dust maker or an extreme pulsating star
cases.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's mid-infrared difference imaging of nearby galaxies (hunt H-0012 v2): a source invisible to Hubble whose infrared light rises sharply every 5.3 years and then settles. Spitzer saw outbursts in 2007, 2012 and 2018, WISE in 2017-18 and 2023. Either a massive binary forming dust at each close approach or an extremely luminous dusty pulsating star; an infrared spectrum would tell. The next outburst is due around mid-2028.

cases.title: A luminous star in NGC 55 lost two-thirds of its infrared glow in 2010-2024 while staying the same in visible light
cases.hook: Found by Oddsky's failed-supernova search (hunt H-0012 v2), but not a failed supernova: the mid-infrared light faded threefold over 14 years while Hubble shows the blue, luminous star unchanged. Its dust is clearing.

cases.title: A hidden source in NGC 4945 that has flared in the infrared every 5.4 years: three outbursts with a sudden rise
cases.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's search for repeating infrared sources in nearby galaxies (hunt H-0013): WISE sees cycles peaking in 2011, 2016-17 and 2022, and Spitzer caught the 2016 rise, a jump of 25x in under half a year. Nothing is catalogued at the position. Next peak expected around 2027.5.

cases.title: A source in NGC 3344 next to Wolf-Rayet stars that flares in the infrared about every 10 years, like the dust maker WR 140
cases.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's search for repeating infrared sources (hunt H-0013): sharp infrared outbursts in 2004, 2014 and 2023, each lasting about a year and a half over a flat minimum, on a young star cluster whose spectrum shows Wolf-Rayet features. Next outburst expected around 2033.

cases.title: Two large infrared eruptions 14 years apart in an HII region of M81, the second in 2024
cases.hook: Found by Oddsky's infrared searches of nearby galaxies (hunts H-0012 and H-0013): an obscured source in M81 erupted by 2009 and again in 2023-24, each time reaching about 3e5 L_sun in the infrared, with nothing seen between.

cases.title: HM Sagittae: the symbiotic nova of 1975, fifty years on
cases.hook: A Mira and a white dwarf that erupted in 1975 and never quite came back; its I band fell 1.5 mag in 2021-22 (Goldman et al. 2022) and the archives now hold four more years.

cases.title: BD+28 4177: the B giant whose infrared excess vanished across the WISE gap
cases.hook: In 2010-11 WISE saw this B0.5 giant 2.3x brighter at 3.4 microns and 14x at 22; since 2014 it is a bare photosphere. Found by hunt H-0016.

agent_meta.harness: Claude Code subagents (5 parallel, 2 packets each), Oddsky CLI in blind mode
agent_meta.tools: oddsky 0.2.0 at commit eac42b3, the code the first two investigators ran (installed outside the repository)
agent_meta.notes: Run two weeks after the first two investigators, on the same packets, prompt and tool version. The answers were already revealed in the repository by then; the investigators worked on copies of the packets outside it and were told not to read anything else (honour system, as before). Self-reported deviations: shell text filters (grep, head, cut) and two python one-liners to trim JSON output for reading, no analysis; deliberately invalid calls to discover argument names; one harness-saved output file of its own tool output read back (T01); one tool output redirected to a scratch file (T06); T05 and T06 bundle several low-probability classes into one entry. Recognised (self-reported): R Cyg (T01, probable), ASASSN-21qj (T03, probable), R CrB (T04), SS Cyg (T06 and H02, probable), Boyajian's Star (T07, probable), AA Tau (T08, possible), EE Cep (H01, probable).

summary.contamination_note: self-reported: did the investigator think it recognised the star? Famous stars leak through blinding; scores on unrecognised packets are the cleaner measure.
summary.baseline_note: uniform guessing over 11 classes: top1 0.091, brier 0.909

For SS Cyg, ~1,000 quiescent points per outburst night pushed real outbursts (V = 8.85) below that cutoff, so 'at least one outburst brighter than 9.3' was graded false although the outburst happened. v2 uses the extreme nightly median. Changed after the reveal, so both gradings are published; only H02 P1 and P2 differ.

agent_meta.harness: Claude Code subagents (4 parallel, 2 packets each, one blind and one hindsight), Oddsky CLI in blind mode
agent_meta.notes: Honour-system blinding (CLI, not MCP); packets were copied outside the repository. The run was interrupted: the machine's disk filled about two minutes in and every command failed. At that point T02 and T04 were complete; T01 had its claims but no hypotheses; T03, H01 and H03 had tool calls but no claims, hypotheses or forecasts; H02 and H04 were unopened. Space was freed and the same four investigators were resumed; three picked up where they stopped. No hypothesis or forecast recorded before the interruption was changed afterwards. One breach after the restart: the H03 investigator had lost its command line, listed the repository's top level and the trial directory (file names only) and re-read the prompt, then redid H03 from the start in the repository's copy of the packet (author strings "probe" and "claude-fable-5-2" in that ledger). It reports opening no answer, case or data file, which cannot be verified; nothing of its forecasts was on record before the interruption. The 14 calls from before the interruption are kept in H03-interrupted/. Other self-reported deviations: output trimmed with tr, head, cut, grep and sed, and shell loops for repeated calls, no analysis scripts; T02's confidences sum to 0.97 because one hypothesis call was refused. Tool problem: lens_fit and eclipse_period reject a series given as a plain string; Fable found the list form on T01, T03 and H02 but not on H01, where it ran no lens fit. Recognised (self-reported): none of the scored stars. It thought H04, an open-question packet, was possibly ASASSN-21qj and says that coloured its forecast probabilities there. It is not that star.

summary.contamination_note: self-reported: did the investigator think it recognised the star? Famous stars leak through blinding; scores on unrecognised packets are the cleaner measure.
summary.baseline_note: uniform guessing over 12 classes: top1 0.083, brier 0.917
